speaker: Other
text: Whereas the Office of the Municipal Clerk, a time-honored and vital part of local government, exists throughout the world, and whereas the Office of the Municipal Clerk is the oldest among public servants, and whereas the Office of the Municipal Clerk provides the professional link between the citizens, the local governing bodies, and agencies of government at other levels, and whereas Municipal Clerks have pledged to be ever-mindful of their neutrality and partiality, rendering equal service to all, and whereas the Municipal Clerk serves as the information center on functions of local government and community, and whereas Municipal Clerks continually strive to improve the administration of the affairs of the Office of the Municipal Clerk through participation in education programs, seminars, workshops, and the annual meetings of their state, province, county, and international professional organizations, and whereas it is most appropriate that we recognize the accomplishments of the Office of the Municipal Clerk, now, therefore, I, Armando Pavoni, Mayor of the City of Renton, do hereby proclaim the week of May 2nd through the 8th, 2021, to be Municipal Clerks Week. In the City of Renton, and further extend appreciation to our Municipal Clerk, Jason Seth, and to all Municipal Clerks for the vital services they perform and their exemplary dedication to the communities they represent. In witness whereof, I have hereunto set my hand and cause the seal of the City of Renton to be affixed this third day of May, 2021. Signed, Armando Pavoni, Mayor, City of Renton. Mr. Mayor?

speaker: Other
text: Good evening, Mr. Mayor, Council President, Council members. My name is Amanda Askren with the Community and Economic Development team. Tonight I am doing a public hearing for the WSDOT acquisition for the I-405 and SR-167 flyover. That is so graciously called. So it is located just south of 405 and on the east side of 167 in the red area shown on the map. This is part of the ongoing 405 widening and express tow lane project that you guys are familiar with. This request is focused just on the area in the 167 and 405. Construction started on this area in 2016, and the city was in previous discussions with WSDOT starting back in 2015 and ongoing, and this is the finalization of the required documents for that construction. There are six city-owned parcels that are involved in the four acquisitions, and then we also did research to determine how those properties were purchased or dedicated to the city to make sure that the funds were allocated appropriately back into the correct account. The first property acquisition is a TCE, a temporary construction easement. It covers parcels A, B, C, D, and F, and as shown in blue, it's a little hard to see. It's between the teal and the green. It's basically a strip running through the middle of that, and then there's some also on the right side of the green. There's $45,145 per feet. The funds are split between the general fund and capital assets depending on which parcel and what square footage. The second property acquisition is a utility easement for parcels C and F, which is shown in orange. This is for the Olympic pipeline that was moved during the construction, so it's to put the easement on top of the pipeline for the post-construction. Both of these parcels are the capital asset properties, so the money would be going to that account. Property acquisition is for a drainage easement, which is the giant green area, which is currently the flail and the restoration that was done in that area, which is on parcels A, B, C, D, and F. The funds are split between the general fund and the capital assets depending on square footage on that parcel. The last one is the property acquisition by deed. This part we're actually giving to WSDOT on A, B, C, D, and F, which is shown in teal, which is the property adjacent to the highway. There's also a utility easement reservation that is the solid teal area located on parcel F that we paid $100 for to keep, which is our pipe running underneath 167, so we have easement on top of that to maintain that. So the funds on this one were also split between the general fund and capital assets depending on square footage and the parcel. So the one that I can't show in a picture is that WSDOT also included compensation for damages in the amount of $13,900, and this was based on the appraisal value from 2015 and the appraisal value now. It dropped due to the construction on the property, so this is just the damages to make a toll of where we were back in 2015 of what was appraised at that time. The total compensation is set at $72,300, and that is for the temporary construction easement, utility easement, drainage easement, the deed, and the damages. So it's split between the general fund and the capital assets. And to note, the temporary construction easement will terminate on November 30th, 2023. Community and Economic Development recommends that the council approve the mayor and the city clerk to execute the WSDOT documents for these acquisitions and also to authorize accepting compensation from WSDOT. So the next steps would be, if you approve, we will work on getting them signed and back to WSDOT for signature and recording on their end and then also accept the compensation from WSDOT. That is the WSDOT.

speaker: Other
text: Do you have one hand? Carmen Rivera? Carmen, go ahead. Hi, my name is Carmen Rivera. I'm a Renton resident, and I am speaking again regarding Officer Trevor Davidson. In the week since I've spoken with you, an e-mail was received by Renton Police Department Interim Chief John Schultz that explained the investigation to Trevor Davidson's association with the known Proud Boy leader Ethan Nordean. It was completed by the Renton Police Department commander. The Discipline Review Board consisted of Renton Police Department's two commanders and one sergeant. And the only thing that was concluded from the investigation is that he was in violation of not reporting that he was in a business venture. And the only consequence he received was a written reprimand, which is pretty much next to nothing. The first problem with the investigation is that they only focused on the fact that the Renton Police Department's policy states that members are prohibited from associating with individuals or groups that are involved in felonies or criminal behavior, which is very limiting. And because we understand our criminal justice system is very subjective, and there are people who are disproportionately represented in that criminal justice system and people who also can get away with a lot of things. Second, and to that point, Ethan Nordean's alias was not included in that investigation, so it is yet to be known if his alias was found guilty of any criminal charges. Furthermore, concluding to the fact that the investigation is shaky at best, and investigations into police personnel shouldn't be conducted by police. We understand that it's a huge conflict of interest. A second problem is that the story that was given, the narration that was given in this email regarding or in the investigation that was explained in this email, the story was inconsistent. See, there was a story that came out in February 2021 that another commander reported that Davidson said that he met Nordean in 2017. And that same story then reported a witness came forward and said that they had seen Ethan Nordean and Trevor Davidson together on several occasions prior to 2017. So then the investigation comes out, and Trevor Davidson then admits that he had known Nordean since 2014. This is inconsistent and shows that either Davidson was lying or someone had the wrong information. Either way, it looks very bad. And then the second part is that Trevor Davidson claims that he didn't understand the extent or knew that the Proud Boys were a known hate group. He just thought that they were a, I think it was a social conservative group, which is laughable to me if you have been following just the daily news as I imagine Trevor Davidson have done. See, this investigation, your people who did the investigation only looked for what they wanted to see. And it was poorly done from what I've been able to read. And it needs to be reopened. And you need to look back into Trevor Davidson. And it shouldn't be limited to only his involvement with someone who has a criminal activity. Because his involvement in business with a known Proud Boy leader, someone who got national notoriety for a major knockout punch in Oregon. A man who gained national notoriety from a Proud Boy leader and has been a known Proud Boy Seattle leader for years. He's been out and proud about this. And you're going to tell me that Officer Trevor Davidson didn't know this about his business partner? And didn't know that the Proud Boys were an extremist hate group that showed up to LGBTQ reading hours with drag queens? They show up to these events filled with beautiful joy with guns? Weren't PDs who showed up and did nothing to the fact that there were Proud Boys at this drag queen story hour protesting a lovely event with guns? Just like our PD didn't do anything about the fact that there was a pistol at our Stanford justice protest just a couple Saturdays ago. Our PD needs some internal investigations to be done into their practices on how they handle the Proud Boys and any other affiliations they may have. Furthermore, we understand the Proud Boys have been recognized as an FBI hate group. And so maybe our PD needs to change its policies that your officers shouldn't have associations with anybody who are part of any known hate group. Rather than being selective in how they're investigating their officers and finding ways just to give them a little slap on the wrist. Again, your safe space program will not be effective if, again, you're going to have police officers who can have businesses and affiliations with known Proud Boy leaders with no consequence. Because, again, I'm not going to call 911 ever as long as I know that Trevor Davidson is an officer with them. So I really hope you take this seriously and ask for a new independent investigation to be done. Thank you. Next person is the Renton Chamber of Commerce. Go ahead. Thank you very much. I just wanted to quickly jump on here. I'm Diane Dobson, CEO of the Renton Chamber of Commerce. And give kudos and accolades to Teresa Nishi and her whole department who put on the most magnificent volunteer appreciation reception and recognition this past week. There was nothing left unturned. She did an absolutely magnificent job. The engagement on the Zoom platform for the volunteers, some of which who haven't seen each other in over a year, was beautiful, heartwarming, and touching. And nothing less than what I would come to expect from the staff there at the City of Renton. Council, I know many of you played a part in it. Mr. Mayor and Chief Van Valey, I know you did, too, as well. So thank you to everyone for continuing to do that outreach. I know in our breakout session, we had over 200 years of service. And that was just in one group that was recognized that night. So thanks for the continued work that you do. You are appreciated. I see no other hands raised, Mr. Mayor.
